content.content:
Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against qqmrtwor, then squvoxyr; nothing runs, and no behaviour is probed.

(1) Subject. A decision whose content is still a placeholder, or which otherwise records no commitment, leaves the check with no subject to read; that absence is a finding, named as such.

(2) The colour role the outline takes (qqmrtwor). That decision records one colour-role row for the focused and selected element: the accent role, at the value and through the token the row names. The dependent's stated focus appearance must take up that same row rather than define a colour of its own. Fail on any element that gives the focused entry a different colour role, substitutes another value or a literal colour for the recorded token, points the accent role at a different token, re-points the recorded token at another role or value, or changes the role that decision assigns to the focused and selected element; name the element and the field of that row it departs from.

(3) The entry that takes the outline (squvoxyr). The thing whose appearance under focus the dependent states is the ref-path entry as squvoxyr records it — presented as a visible link rather than as bare text — and the outline is presentation over that entry, not a re-decision of it. Fail on any element that attaches the outline to something other than that entry (its bare text, an icon, or a row or region holding several entries), that withholds, replaces or competes with the entry's link presentation while the outline is shown, that makes the entry inert or otherwise deprives it of the presentation as a visible link, or that states a rule only that decision states: what the entry is, its label or body, its place in the panel's section, or what activating it does — an activation input or variant, a transport, message or command, a file or path resolution or normalization rule, or behaviour for a path that names no file — including an activation provoked by focus itself rather than by the activation the entry is recorded to have. If that decision carries no recorded commitment about such an entry, the use has nothing to be read against, and that absence is a finding.

(4) Focus bound. The commitment must bind the outline to the state it names: the outline is the entry's appearance while the entry holds focus, so its presence and absence follow that state and no other. Fail if the dependent records no such bound, if the recorded appearance holds independently of focus — always shown, or shown on hover, on selection or on activation instead — or if the outline is stated for a focus variant or focus condition the dependent leaves unrecorded.

(5) Non-contradiction and decidability. No element of the dependent contradicts qqmrtwor or squvoxyr; fail on any contradicting element, naming it and the prerequisite involved. From the recorded statement alone a reviewer must be able to name an observation that would refute it without supplying a rule the dependent does not state — an entry holding focus shown without the accent focus outline, an accent focus outline shown while focus is elsewhere, or a focused entry presented as something other than the visible link that decision records. If no such observation can be named from the statement, that is a finding.
content.rationale:
The dependent is an inline prose commitment, so it is natural-layer. squvoxyr is inline prose too — natural-to-natural, the evaluation matrix's gate cell. qqmrtwor is an inline visual-spec, a structured parent used by a natural child, a cell no eval-matrix row covers, so it takes the default cell: the gate form, flagged for a matrix entry. Both edges are read by a reviewer applying the criterion to the recorded nodes and nothing runs: the child is prose, so the strictness rule denies behaviour probes, and a runnable check of an appearance commitment would have to invent the observable the dependent is free to state differently — that belongs to an edge whose child is code.

Non-violation alone would leave the two ways this decision can go wrong ungated. First, an appearance commitment can say "accent" and mean a highlight of its own: a second accent definition, a literal colour, another token, or an accent role re-pointed away from the token qqmrtwor records, none of which contradicts that record in so many words while the focused entry stops matching the workbench focus treatment the row exists to keep. Second, presentation is easy to state and mean more: attaching the outline to the row or the surrounding region rather than to the entry, withdrawing the entry's link rendering while it is outlined, or sliding an activation in behind the focus — focus itself opening what the entry presents, or a path rule arriving with the appearance — which re-decides what squvoxyr records. The criteria therefore keep the two uses apart rather than checking for surface contradiction: against qqmrtwor, the outline's colour role is the recorded row and not a new one; against squvoxyr, the outlined thing is the entry that decision records, and neither what it is nor what activating it does is re-decided. Clause (4) holds the commitment to the state it names, so a decision that leaves the outline independent of holding focus cannot pass by picks. Clause (5) keeps the whole commitment decidable at review time.

Every clause is decidable by reading three recorded nodes, names no endpoint-specific element in advance — which element or field fails is the check's output, never the criterion — demands no wording, layout, metric or mechanism of the dependent, and states no rule its prerequisites do not, so it survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides.
